rationale: Evidence from iteration 3 (kp 3.0, kd 0.6, base_speed 1.0, iteration 0 sensor layout) is the best raced design so far at 458.0, up from 169.5. Oval now finishes 20 of 20 runs with progress 0.997, a mean score of 956, and line-loss events of 0.1. The gain from kd 0.4 to 0.6 was large and monotonic on the failing tracks: s-bend progress rose from 0.28 to 0.72 and slalom from 0.13 to 0.23. Line-loss events on the s-bend also fell from 1.05 to 1.0. The remaining failures are off-track ends with max_error still at the 0.06 m limit (s-bend 0.0612, slalom 0.0632). Slalom is the weakest track (0 of 20 finishes, progress 0.23). Changing kd from 0.4 to 0.6 did not bring max_error below 0.06, so the feedback rule 'keep kd 0.6 and raise base_speed' does not apply, because the s-bend has not yet reached a stable margin. The feedback's alternative of adding ki is a different hypothesis. I choose a single-variable step that follows the observed trend: kd 0.6 to 0.8, with kp 3.0, ki 0, base_speed 1.0 and the sensor layout held fixed. kd is the lever that has improved progress on every failing track so far, and the bend overshoot it damps is the likely source of the off-track exits. Speed is kept at 1.0 because the s-bend finish time (2.97 s) is already near the 3.0 s limit, so raising speed now risks the completions that are the main score. Expected result: s-bend and slalom progress rise further, with max_error below about 0.06 on at least the s-bend, and oval finishes held. Main risk: steering_oscillation has grown with kd (oval 0.24 at kd 0.6, s-bend 0.45), so kd 0.8 could add jitter and reduce progress on the oval. Hypotheses to check next: (a) if s-bend and slalom progress rise and oval still finishes, kd is still improving and the next step is base_speed 1.2 to recover time; (b) if progress falls or oscillation rises sharply, kd 0.6 is the peak and I should return to it and test ki 0.05 to 0.1 for the residual bend error; (c) if max_error on the slalom stays at about 0.063 with line losses near 1.5, the slalom's tight alternating bends need a different lever (kp or sensor spacing) rather than more kd. Measurements requested: completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation and control_effort on all three tracks.
